workflow.title: Inspect a Mac app before replacing a duplicate build
workflow.primaryIntent: Understand versions, architectures and app metadata before choosing which installed copy to keep, without treating framework choice as a performance benchmark.
workflow.reader: Mac owners and developers with apparently duplicate app bundles or unexplained launch differences
workflow.conclusion: Use documented metadata inspection for what a bundle is; use runtime measurements for what it is doing. Neither framework labels nor duplicate status alone authorize deletion.
outline: Identify the installed copies and preserve original data
Separate version/architecture/framework metadata from runtime CPU and memory
What AppVoid documents: inspection and launch diagnostics (vendor claims, not hands-on)
Duplicate build decision checklist: compatibility, original source, current use and backup before any replacement
Where Breathing Room's grouped app view answers a different question
Limitations: store availability, IAP split, preview status and missing measurements
workflow.visualPlan: AppVoid official app image after lead once rights/content inspection passes; selected Breathing Room Apps preview beside metadata-versus-runtime explanation with required example-data caption.
workflow.interactionHandoff: Non-mutating decision checklist: metadata question / live-resource question / duplicate-copy question; final step is review, never a deletion button. No invented scan or savings calculator.
mustNotClaim: Intel builds are always safe to trash
Private API detection means malware detection
Breathing Room replaces AppVoid's app-internals inspection
workflow.disclosure: Breathing Room, which we build; one bounded recommendation only.
